details:
FIREMIND — Intelligent Fire Activity Harmonization

Project Description

FIREMIND is a geospatial intelligence platform designed to address a major challenge in satellite-based fire monitoring: the differences between MODIS and VIIRS active-fire observations.

Although both satellite systems detect active fires, their observations differ in spatial resolution, detection characteristics, and observation patterns. These differences make their records difficult to compare directly, creating inconsistencies in long-term fire activity analysis.

FIREMIND addresses this problem through a data-driven harmonization pipeline.

Our workflow organizes satellite observations using H3 spatial indexing and weekly temporal aggregation, creating consistent geographic and temporal units. A machine learning model then uses MODIS-derived features to estimate VIIRS-equivalent fire counts, with NOAA-20 VIIRS observations serving as a comparison reference.

The resulting data powers an interactive dashboard that allows users to:

  • Explore historical fire activity across geographic areas.
  • Visualize fire hotspots and their spatial distribution.
  • Navigate weekly fire activity patterns.
  • Identify unusual activity and deviations from expected patterns.
  • Examine individual H3 geographic cells.
  • Compare model estimates with reference observations.
  • Inspect calibrated uncertainty intervals alongside estimated values.

Benefits and Intended Impact

FIREMIND aims to make satellite-derived fire observations more consistent, accessible, and useful for understanding fire activity over time.

Its main benefits include:

Improved Data Comparability: Establishes a consistent analytical framework for examining observations from different satellite systems.

Historical Fire Analysis: Helps users investigate long-term fire activity, recurring patterns, and periods of increased burning.

Unusual Activity Detection: Highlights deviations from expected fire activity to support further investigation.

Geographic Intelligence: Enables users to examine fire activity across different locations and spatial scales.

Transparent Uncertainty: Presents uncertainty alongside model estimates instead of treating predictions as exact satellite observations.

Our intended impact is to support researchers, environmental organizations, land managers, and fire-monitoring professionals with more consistent information for understanding historical fire activity and identifying important patterns.

Tools and Technologies

FIREMIND combines programming, geospatial processing, machine learning, and web development.

  • Python: Data processing, analytical workflows, and machine learning development.
  • JavaScript: Interactive dashboard functionality and data visualization.
  • HTML: Dashboard structure.
  • CSS: Interface styling and layout.
  • H3 Geospatial Indexing: Organizing observations into consistent geographic cells.
  • NASA FIRMS: Active-fire satellite observations.
  • MODIS: Historical active-fire observations.
  • VIIRS NOAA-20: Reference observations for harmonization and model evaluation.

Creativity and Innovation

FIREMIND goes beyond conventional fire hotspot visualization.

Its central innovation is addressing differences between satellite observation systems through a machine learning approach that estimates VIIRS-equivalent fire counts using MODIS-derived features.

Rather than assuming that observations from different satellites are directly interchangeable, FIREMIND establishes consistent spatial and temporal units before performing estimation.

The platform combines this harmonization approach with historical exploration, unusual activity detection, geographic visualization, and uncertainty analysis in one interactive environment.

We also compare our machine learning approach against a seasonal-ratio baseline using held-out testing. This provides a measurable way to evaluate the model against a simpler alternative rather than relying solely on visual results.

Factors Considered During Development

Several factors guided our development:

Scientific Reliability: Distinguishing actual satellite observations from machine learning estimates.

Satellite Differences: Accounting for differences in spatial resolution and detection characteristics.

Spatial and Temporal Consistency: Using standardized geographic cells and weekly aggregation.

Model Uncertainty: Communicating the limitations and uncertainty associated with estimated fire counts.

Accessibility: Making complex geospatial information understandable through an interactive interface.

Practical Feasibility: Developing a solution capable of processing satellite datasets and presenting meaningful analytical results through a web application.

Conclusion

FIREMIND transforms fragmented satellite fire observations into a more coherent analytical framework. By combining geospatial harmonization, machine learning, and interactive visualization, it helps users understand not only where fires are detected, but also how burning activity evolves across locations and over time.

FIREMIND — See the signal. Understand the gaps.
